newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-TURKISH TEAM PROTESTS AT FREELOADERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TURKISH TEAM PROTESTS AT FREELOADERS.

text.p: Turkish team Altay on Monday called on sports officials to act against "freeloaders" who get into big matches by stealing tickets, breaking the turnstiles or being let in by friends working at the stadium.

Altay chairman Erdinc Altinyeleklioglu told the Anatolian news agency his club had lost billions of lira (thousands of dollars) after 60,000 people watched the Izmir team's weekend tie against league leaders Galatasaray although only 36,663 tickets had been sold.
"In no country in the world do you have more than 10,000 freeloaders," Altinyeleklioglu said. "We had a deal with a security firm to prevent freeloaders. But we failed."
The sports ministry's Izmir representative, Bahri Vreskala, said 103 million lira ($1,080) worth of tickets had been stolen before the Galatasaray match and that some turnstiles had been broken.
Officials at Turkish sports meetings are always ready to let friends and relatives in free, and the organisers of most events regularly send out dozens of invitations to friends and colleagues.
